Athena user guide

Athena is a self-hosted control panel for your home server. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, and shows only what your machine supports.

Contents

  1. Getting started: install, first sign-in, upgrade, uninstall
  2. Dashboard: live stats and your apps
  3. Apps and the store: install from the store or from your own compose file
  4. Packages: host software through apt, Homebrew, winget and others
  5. Files and sharing: file manager, share links, WebDAV and SMB
  6. Cloud storage: Google Drive, OneDrive, S3 and more through rclone
  7. Containers and terminal
  8. AI assistant
  9. Automation: cron, webhooks and the MCP server
  10. Backups
  11. Remote access and HTTPS
  12. Settings: appearance, account, system, AI
  13. Command line: the athena command
  14. Troubleshooting
  15. Comparison with other panels

Developers: see DEVELOPMENT.md and the design notes in docs/design.

Which pages you see

Athena detects what your host can do (a container runtime, rclone, a package manager, a tunnel tool) and hides what it can't. If a page or button from this guide is missing, that capability isn't available on your machine. The troubleshooting page shows how to find out why.
